subject: Integration follow-up: embeddings + reranker + structured-output reliability

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Moss <oliver.moss@aurelia.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Integration follow-up: embeddings + reranker + structured-output reliability

Hi Oliver —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same runway: 

Recap (what we covered)
- Integration scope: SDK + auth, request routing (latency vs cost tiers), embeddings index + reranker flow.
- Structured output needs: constrained JSON responses for our classification pipeline (fixed schema), tool-calling for enrichment, and validation + retry behavior for malformed outputs.
- Ops ask: observability on token cost per route, latency P95, and per-request schema validation traces.

Immediate next steps (owners + ETA)
1) Send a short integration plan + sample schema examples — owner: me (attached). ETA: EOD Tuesday.
2) Solutions deep-dive on SDK quickstart + auth patterns — owner: Marissa. ETA: Wed next week (30th).
3) Workshop to align reranker latency targets and embedding index strategy — owner: Oliver / Aurelia. Proposed dates: Jun 1 or Jun 3.
4) Validation & retry playbook draft (schema-aware retries + idempotency patterns) — owner: Priyom. ETA: Jun 4.

Attachments: redwood-integration-plan.pdf (high level plan + milestones).

If that looks correct, I’ll book the SRE/Solutions session and share a calendar invite for the workshop.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[dylan.brooks@redwood.ai] | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: embeddings + reranker + structured-output reliability

Dylan —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

1) Embeddings/reranker
- We typically run a dense index with nightly refreshes; for near-real-time content we need on-the-fly reranking. What latencies can we expect for a reranker path vs a pure retrieval-only path? Target P95 for us is sub-120ms on the rerank step.

2) SDK & auth
- We need examples for both API-key usage and a short note on integrating with our Okta-backed OIDC for service-to-service auth. Can Marissa include a token rotation recommendation?

3) Structured-output reliability
- Important: our downstream tooling assumes strict JSON with a fixed key set. If Redwood returns malformed JSON (or out-of-schema) what is your recommended flow? Is constrained decoding + a validator in the SDK the pattern you recommend, or do you prefer server-side enforcement + SDK fallback? Also: do you have examples of schema-guided retries versus just rejecting the call?

4) Data residency / Private option
- We discussed Private (VPC) for PII datasets. Can you include a short note in the plan about what changes from Hosted in terms of audit logs and KMS?

We’re excited to move forward — happy with the proposed workshop dates, Jun 1 works best for our engineering lead.

Thanks —
Oliver Moss
Head of Search & AI, Aurelia Analytics
oliver.moss@aurelia.ai | +44 20 7946 0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Moss <oliver.moss@aurelia.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 May 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: embeddings + reranker + structured-output reliability

Hi Oliver —

Great questions. I pulled together targeted answers below and attached two artifacts: schema-examples.json and validation-playbook.md.

1) Reranker latency
- Typical hosted reranker: 40-120ms P95 depending on model size and payload. For tight targets (sub-120ms) we recommend:
  * Use a smaller, distilled reranker model for live re-rank path (we can ship a verified 350M checkpoint).
  * Route high-priority traffic to Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) to reduce cold-start jitter.
  * Employ dead-man fallback: if reranker latency exceeds threshold, serve retrieval-only ranking to meet SLA.

2) SDK + auth patterns
- SDK quickstart: our SDK supports both API-key header flows and OIDC service account tokens. Example (pseudocode):

  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=ENV.REDSK_API_KEY)  # short-lived key supported
  # or OIDC client credentials
  token = fetch_oidc_token(client_id, client_secret)
  client = RedwoodClient(bearer_token=token)

- Token rotation: recommend short-lived tokens (1h) plus automatic refresh in SDK. For long-lived certs (on-prem) pair with KMS-backed secrets and automated rotation via your secrets manager.

3) Structured output reliability (recommended pattern)
- Multi-layer approach we use in production:
  a) Constrained decoding: add token-level constraints (allowed tokens/seq) for structural delimiters and enumerated fields.
  b) Server-side schema validation: the inference runtime validates model output against the canonical JSON schema before returning to the SDK.
  c) SDK-side validator: the SDK includes a lightweight validator (fast JSON schema check) to catch edge cases and surface rich error codes.
  d) Retry policy: only retry when the validator reports recoverable decode issues (truncated output, stray commas). For semantic violations (field types wrong), don't retry; instead return a structured error with classifier scores for downstream resolution.

- Idempotency: include an idempotency token per user-request so retries are safe. See validation-playbook.md for exact error codes and mapping.

4) Private / VPC notes
- Private deployment provides: customer KMS support (HSM-backed), syslog + audit-forwarding, and VPC-only control plane. Hosted behavior is the default; Private adds audit log retention controls and dedicated network egress.

Attachments: schema-examples.json (sample schemas for the response object) and validation-playbook.md (mapping of errors to retry behavior, idempotency guidance, and backoff recommendations).

Quick notes on implementation timeline
- I can run the SDK quickstart and auth demo in a 60–90 min session. I’ll propose Wed May 30 10:00–11:30 or Fri Jun 1 09:00–10:30 PT.

Let me know what works and I’ll share a calendar invite and short runbook for the session.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0202

Attachment: schema-examples.json (3KB)
Attachment: validation-playbook.md (6KB)
